February 2025Red Rocks Park, Morrison, Colorado

Red Rocks, CO

memories below

Warm Stone

By late February the foothills are mostly straw-colored grass and patches of old snow, under a sky that can't decide between gray and blue. Then a wall of red sandstone takes over. The slabs here are pocked with hollows like honeycomb and freckled with yellow-green lichen. They tell the same story as Roxborough's fins, tipped on edge when the modern Rockies pushed up behind them. The rust, pink and faint purple come from iron in the stone.

I wasn't the only one admiring the wall. A herd of mule deer, five or six at least, was grazing the dry grass at its foot, right beside a trail sign. Their enormous ears swiveled like satellite dishes, and still they paid me no attention. One by one they strolled along the dirt path as if it were their own sidewalk, which in fairness it is. A zoom lens is the polite way to do this.

The evening before, I think, the color had run the other way. On a mountain highway at dusk there were plowed snowbanks, dark spruce, a high ridge holding the last of the light and a pair of tail lights up ahead. Further on, the sky faded to deep blue and then to a thin glow over a black ridgeline. Cold blue one day, warm stone the next.
